headline: Tk 68.76cr loan case: Arrest warrant issued against M Morshed Khan
summary: A Dhaka money loan court has issued warrants against the former foreign minister and four other Citycell officials in a recovery case brought by Mutual Trust Bank.
details: A Dhaka money loan court has issued an arrest warrant against former foreign minister M Morshed Khan, founder and chairman of Citycell, in a loan recovery case brought by Mutual Trust Bank (MTB) PLC.

Warrants were also issued against four other officials of Pacific Bangladesh Telecom Limited (PBTL), the defunct mobile operator known as Citycell: Directors Asghar Karim and Nasreen Khan, Acting CFO Md Farikul Hasan, and CEO Mehboob Chowdhury.

Artha Rin Adalat No. 7 issued the warrants on September 23 under Section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, which allows for civil detention of up to six months for debtors who fail to satisfy a decree.
The court has directed the Gulshan Police Station, via the Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner, to arrest the individuals and produce them in court by November 18.
Mutual Trust Bank filed the case on July 5, 2018, seeking the recovery of Tk 68.76 crore in outstanding dues.
PBTL, Bangladesh's first mobile operator, ceased operations in 2016 after failing to pay dues to the telecom regulator and was listed among the country's top 20 loan defaulters as of December 2025.

Syed Mahbubur Rahman, MD and CEO of Mutual Trust Bank, stated that the bank will use all legal avenues to recover the money, emphasizing that 'nobody is above the law' and that the depositors' money must be recovered.

headline: Banglalink gets nod for limited Starlink service, first in South Asia
summary: BTRC approval allows standard 4G phones to connect directly to satellites, extending connectivity to remote islands, hill tracts, and disaster-hit areas.
details: Banglalink has received approval from the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) to launch a limited Starlink Direct-to-Cell service. This makes Bangladesh the first country in South Asia to introduce this technology.
caption:
No more dead zones. Banglalink is bringing Starlink's satellite connectivity directly to standard 4G phones in Bangladesh.

Banglalink has received approval from the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) to launch a limited Starlink Direct-to-Cell service. This makes Bangladesh the first country in South Asia to introduce this technology.
